packages.title: UK ETS cap and allowance versus emissions QA
facts: The UK ETS uses an overall cap and tradable allowances as a carbon-pricing framework.
Some allowances are allocated for free to mitigate carbon-leakage risks in eligible sectors.
Allowances can be traded on a secondary market.
An allowance holding or market trade is not the same as a measured physical emission.
No parcel emissions quantity is derived from allowance-market activity.

packages.title: UK ETS aviation policy 2026 free-allocation end QA
facts: The UK ETS policy overview states aviation free allocation ended from 1 January 2026.
The policy change is part of the scheme's aviation decarbonisation framework.
Policy coverage and compliance incentives are not direct measurements of flight emissions.
Any emissions result still requires the applicable monitoring and verification evidence.
No parcel-level value is inferred.

packages.title: Smart meters Q1 2026 stock QA
facts: At the end of March 2026, over 41 million smart and advanced meters were in homes and small businesses across Great Britain.
The Q1 report states 72% of all meters were smart or advanced.
Over 38 million were operating in smart mode or classified as advanced meters, corresponding to 66%.
Meter stock and operating-mode counts are rollout metrics, not energy consumption or greenhouse-gas measurements.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from a meter count.

packages.title: Smart meters Q1 2026 installation flow QA
facts: Large energy suppliers installed about 590,000 smart and advanced meters in Q1 2026.
The Q1 installation count was reported as down 1.0% from the previous quarter.
It was reported as down 18% from the same quarter in 2025.
The quarterly report combines current large-supplier data with small-supplier information on a different reporting cadence.
Installation flow does not establish a property's emissions.

packages.title: Smart meters operated versus installed QA
facts: The smart-meter collection reports both meters operating and meters installed.
It covers domestic properties and smaller non-domestic sites.
Large-supplier data are updated quarterly while the broader market has an annual update component.
Installed and operating counts must not be conflated.
Neither count is a direct greenhouse-gas measurement.

packages.title: Smart meters Q2 2026 future-release guard QA
facts: The latest published 2026 quarterly update as of 25 July 2026 is the report to end March 2026.
The April to June 2026 release is scheduled for 27 August 2026.
A scheduled future release is not current observed data.
Q1 values must not be silently extended into Q2.
No future meter count is fabricated.

packages.title: Smart meters National Data Library Q1 dataset QA
facts: The National Data Library lists the Q1 2026 smart-meter dataset added on 28 May 2026.
The dataset is an official-statistics rollout dataset.
It provides meter deployment information rather than household energy-use measurements.
Dataset vintage must be retained when comparing quarters.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from rollout data.

packages.title: Smart-meter rollout versus GHG QA
facts: Smart-meter rollout data describe installed and operating metering infrastructure.
Meter presence does not determine a building's fuel consumption by itself.
Meter presence does not determine a building's greenhouse-gas emissions by itself.
Any emissions calculation would require separate consumption and factor evidence.
No such parcel calculation is performed in this package.

packages.title: EPC Q1 2026 lodgement count QA
facts: About 460,000 EPCs were lodged in England and Wales in January to March 2026 for domestic and non-domestic properties combined.
In England, about 416,000 domestic EPCs were lodged in the quarter.
England recorded about 48,000 new-dwelling EPCs and 368,000 existing-dwelling EPCs in the quarter.
EPC lodgements are register records and do not equal the building stock.
No parcel greenhouse-gas measurement is inferred from a lodgement count.

packages.title: EPC EER and EIR modelled-rating QA
facts: Domestic EPCs report an Energy Efficiency Rating based on estimated fuel costs.
They also report an Environmental Impact Rating based on estimated CO2 emissions.
Both ratings are estimated from property characteristics rather than direct continuous emissions measurement.
The release warns against using the register to count the total building stock.
No EPC band is converted into a parcel emissions quantity here.

packages.title: EPC local-authority allocation revision QA
facts: The Q1 2026 EPC publication was revised after an error in the lookup used to allocate postcodes to local authorities.
The revision affected regional and local-authority allocation more than the main national totals.
Revised records are identified in the published statistics.
Subnational analysis must use the corrected allocation rather than the superseded lookup.
No affected record is silently reassigned without source evidence.

packages.title: EPC April to June 2026 future-release guard QA
facts: The April to June 2026 EPC statistics are scheduled for publication on 30 July 2026.
That date is after the current 25 July 2026 evidence cutoff.
The future release must not be treated as observed.
Q1 values are not projected into Q2.
No future local-authority EPC value is fabricated.

packages.title: Boiler Upgrade Scheme May 2026 uptake QA
facts: The May 2026 Boiler Upgrade Scheme statistics were published on 25 June 2026.
They report voucher applications and redemptions.
They also report installation-cost information for supported low-carbon technologies.
Grant uptake and redemption are programme-delivery metrics rather than direct greenhouse-gas measurements.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from a voucher.

packages.title: Boiler Upgrade Scheme geography and measure scope QA
facts: The May 2026 Boiler Upgrade Scheme release applies to England and Wales.
The scheme statistics concern capital-grant uptake for low-carbon technology installations.
Installation and voucher records must retain their programme geography.
An installed technology count is not identical to measured energy savings or emissions reductions.
No property-level emissions amount is created.

packages.title: Boiler Upgrade Scheme provisional-series QA
facts: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme collection provides monthly and cumulative analyses.
The collection states the statistics are provisional and subject to future revision.
The latest release listed as of the evidence date is May 2026.
Provisional programme counts should not be treated as immutable final values.
No future June 2026 result is assumed.

packages.title: BUS applications versus redemptions QA
facts: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme series distinguishes voucher applications from redemptions.
An application count and a redemption count represent different programme stages.
Installation costs are another separate programme metric.
None of these programme metrics by themselves measures greenhouse-gas emissions.
No parcel emissions estimate is inferred from programme stage.
